Help Ms. Suzuki find her cat
Ms. Suzuki's cat Mike has been missing since yesterday. Ask about it, understand the description and offer to help.
Meet Ms. Suzuki
Understand what Mike looks like
Offer to help find the cat
Ah... excuse me. Have you seen my cat?
No, I haven't. What does the cat look like?
I haven't seen it.
I like cats.
I see... Mike is a calico cat: white, brown and black. She's been missing since yesterday.
Ah, thank you... But my cat has gone missing now...
Her name is Mike. She's a calico cat, white, brown and black.
She has a red ribbon on her neck. She's not a big cat. She's small.
Did you get that? What colour is Mike?
She's white, brown and black.
Could you say that once more, please?
She's a white cat.
Yes. White, brown, black. Three colours. That's Mike.
Not just white. White, brown and black. Three colours.
That's right! What does Mike have on her neck?
A red ribbon.
A blue bell.
Could you say that once more, please?
No. It's a red ribbon. She has a red ribbon on her neck.
Yes. On her neck, a red ribbon. I tied it on her myself yesterday.
Last night I opened the window. Since then, Mike has been gone.
Since when has she been missing?
When?
Where?
"Doko" asks about a place. To ask about time, use "itsu".
Since about eight last night. It's been twenty hours already.
Mike often goes near the shrine. She also likes the park.
Near the shrine. I understand.
The park. I understand.
I don't like shrines.
Ah... I see. But Mike loves the shrine. Please listen once more.
Oh, what should I do... I wonder if Mike is cold.
Shall I help you look for her?
Good luck.
The cat will come back on her own.
Thank you... But on my own it's a bit... hard.
I... see. But I'm really worried.
Really! Thank you, thank you so much!
If you see Mike, please tell me. My house is the one with the blue roof over there.
Yes, if I see her I'll tell you right away.
Yes, probably.
No, I'm busy.
Yes... I'm counting on you.
Huh... a moment ago you said "I'll help you look"...
Thank you. I'm sure Mike will be very happy too.
Summary: "donna ~ desu ka" (what kind of ~?), "~ masen deshita" (did not ~), "~ mashou ka" (shall I ~?). Keep an eye on the shrine and the park on your walks!
